# truenas_ftp_config (Data Source)

Reads the current `ftp` settings. Secrets are not exposed.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `anonpath` (String) Filesystem path for anonymous FTP users. `null` to use the default anonymous FTP directory.
- `anonuserbw` (Number) Maximum upload bandwidth in KiB/s for anonymous users. 0 means unlimited.
- `anonuserdlbw` (Number) Maximum download bandwidth in KiB/s for anonymous users. 0 means unlimited.
- `banner` (String) Welcome message displayed to FTP clients upon connection.
- `clients` (Number) Maximum number of simultaneous client connections allowed.
- `defaultroot` (Boolean) Whether to restrict users to their home directories (chroot jail).
- `dirmask` (String) Default Unix permissions (umask) for directories created by FTP users.
- `filemask` (String) Default Unix permissions (umask) for files created by FTP users.
- `fxp` (Boolean) Whether to enable File eXchange Protocol (FXP) for server-to-server transfers.
- `id` (Number) Identifier assigned by TrueNAS.
- `ident` (Boolean) Whether to perform RFC 1413 ident lookups on connecting clients.
- `ipconnections` (Number) Maximum number of connections allowed from a single IP address. 0 means unlimited.
- `localuserbw` (Number) Maximum upload bandwidth in KiB/s for local users. 0 means unlimited.
- `localuserdlbw` (Number) Maximum download bandwidth in KiB/s for local users. 0 means unlimited.
- `loginattempt` (Number) Maximum number of failed login attempts before blocking an IP address. 0 disables this limit.
- `masqaddress` (String) Public IP address to advertise to clients for passive mode connections when behind NAT.
- `onlyanonymous` (Boolean) Whether to allow only anonymous FTP access, disabling authenticated user login.
- `onlylocal` (Boolean) Whether to allow only local system users to login, disabling anonymous access.
- `options` (String) Additional ProFTPD configuration directives to include in the server configuration.     Manual directives may render the FTP service non-functional and should be used with caution.
- `passiveportsmax` (Number) Maximum port number for passive mode data connections. Must be 0 or between 1024-65535.
- `passiveportsmin` (Number) Minimum port number for passive mode data connections. Must be 0 or between 1024-65535.
- `port` (Number) TCP port number on which the FTP service listens for incoming connections.
- `resume` (Boolean) Whether to allow clients to resume interrupted file transfers.
- `reversedns` (Boolean) Whether to perform reverse DNS lookups on client IP addresses for logging.
- `ssltls_certificate` (Number) ID of the certificate to use for TLS/SSL connections. `null` to use the default system certificate.
- `timeout` (Number) Idle timeout in seconds before disconnecting inactive clients. 0 disables timeout.
- `timeout_notransfer` (Number) Timeout in seconds for clients that connect but do not transfer data. 0 disables timeout.
- `tls` (Boolean) Whether to enable TLS/SSL encryption for FTP connections.
- `tls_opt_allow_client_renegotiations` (Boolean) Whether to allow TLS clients to initiate renegotiation of the TLS connection.
- `tls_opt_allow_dot_login` (Boolean) Whether to allow .ftpaccess files to override TLS requirements for specific users.
- `tls_opt_allow_per_user` (Boolean) Whether to allow per-user TLS configuration overrides.
- `tls_opt_common_name_required` (Boolean) Whether to require client certificates to have a Common Name field.
- `tls_opt_dns_name_required` (Boolean) Whether to require client certificates to contain a DNS name in the Subject Alternative Name extension.     The `reversedns` setting must also be enabled.
- `tls_opt_enable_diags` (Boolean) Whether to enable detailed TLS diagnostic logging.
- `tls_opt_export_cert_data` (Boolean) Whether to export client certificate data to environment variables.
- `tls_opt_ip_address_required` (Boolean) Whether to require client certificates to contain an IP address in the Subject Alternative Name extension.
- `tls_opt_no_empty_fragments` (Boolean) Whether to disable empty TLS record fragments to improve compatibility with some clients.      Disabling increases vulnerability to some attack vectors.
- `tls_opt_no_session_reuse_required` (Boolean) Whether to disable the requirement for TLS session reuse.
- `tls_opt_stdenvvars` (Boolean) Whether to export standard TLS environment variables for use by external programs.
- `tls_policy` (String) TLS policy for connections. Values include: `"on"` (required), `"off"` (disabled), `"data"` (data only),     `"auth"` (authentication only), `"ctrl"` (control only), or combinations with `+` and `!` modifiers.
